metadata.name: Beyond HYPE Final Research Dataset
metadata.purpose: Interactive industry-change → work-change → role-change → capability → build → evidence system
metadata.note: Claims are deliberately separated from interpretation; layoffs are not treated as proof of AI replacement without evidence.

fields.description: Building, shipping and operating software systems.
fields.current_landscape: AI-assisted development, cloud-native systems, distributed systems, automation and stronger end-to-end ownership.
fields.primary_evidence: Stack Overflow 2025; Amazon SDE India 2027; GitHub Octoverse 2025

fields.description: Developing and deploying machine-learning and AI systems.
fields.current_landscape: Production ML, GenAI/LLMs, large-scale data, evaluation, deployment and AI-enabled products.
fields.primary_evidence: Amazon Applied Scientist India 2027; TCS AI Careers 2026; WEF 2025

fields.description: Turning data into reliable analysis, products and decisions.
fields.current_landscape: Data platforms, pipelines, cloud warehouses/lakes, analytics, ML-ready data and data quality.

fields.description: Protecting applications, infrastructure, identities, data and AI systems.
fields.current_landscape: Cloud security, application security, AI security, risk, detection/response and governance.

fields.description: Building and operating reliable cloud infrastructure and delivery systems.
fields.current_landscape: Cloud-native architecture, containers/Kubernetes, automation, observability, platform engineering and AI infrastructure.
fields.primary_evidence: CNCF research; Amazon cloud roles 2026-27; WEF 2025

industry_changes.change: AI-assisted software development
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Code generation, documentation, testing and learning are increasingly integrated into developer workflows.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: AI assistance is widespread, but trust and verification remain active constraints.

industry_changes.change: Cloud-native and distributed systems remain core
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Modern software roles increasingly involve scalable cloud services, microservices and distributed systems.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: Current India SDE postings explicitly mention cloud-native architectures, microservices and resilient distributed systems.

industry_changes.change: End-to-end ownership is becoming more visible
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Intern and early-career roles increasingly describe design-through-deployment and operations, not only coding.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: This widens the capability set expected from software engineers.

industry_changes.change: AI does not remove the need for verification
industry_changes.what_is_happening: AI adoption is high, but developers report distrust, near-correct outputs and debugging costs.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: The useful shift is toward assisted production plus human verification.

industry_changes.change: Developer ecosystems are expanding and changing
industry_changes.what_is_happening: GitHub reports continued growth in developers and AI-related repositories, while language usage is shifting.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: Open-source activity is a useful technology signal, not a direct measure of hiring demand.

industry_changes.change: AI is moving from experiments toward enterprise systems
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Organizations are investing in enterprise AI, GenAI, agents and AI-enabled operations.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: The work is increasingly about integrating AI into real products and workflows.

industry_changes.change: Production ML requires more than model training
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Current applied-science roles combine models with data, experimentation, system design and production deployment.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: Students need both ML knowledge and engineering ability.

industry_changes.change: AI specialization is widening
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Agentic AI, ML engineering, MLOps and AI infrastructure are distinct areas of work.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: These are specializations, not guarantees of job growth for every student.

industry_changes.change: Evaluation becomes central
industry_changes.what_is_happening: As AI systems generate outputs, teams need to test quality, reliability and failure modes.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: Evaluation is a practical bridge between research and production.
industry_changes.source: Stack Overflow 2025 AI; Amazon Applied Scientist India 2027

industry_changes.change: AI work is increasingly cross-functional
industry_changes.what_is_happening: AI roles interact with software, data, infrastructure, product and business teams.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: Communication and system thinking therefore sit alongside technical ML skills.
industry_changes.source: Amazon Applied Scientist India 2027; TCS AI Careers 2026

industry_changes.change: Data engineering is increasingly platform-oriented
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Roles cover pipelines, warehouses, lakes, schemas, ETL/ELT and cloud data services.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: Data work is moving beyond spreadsheets toward production data systems.

industry_changes.change: Data quality and validation matter more
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Current data roles explicitly mention integrity, testing, validation and documentation.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: Reliable data is a prerequisite for analytics and ML.

industry_changes.change: Cloud data platforms are mainstream
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Data roles increasingly combine SQL with cloud services, distributed processing and warehouse/lake technologies.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: Students benefit from understanding where data lives and how it moves.

industry_changes.change: Analytics is becoming closer to product decisions
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Data scientists and engineers are expected to create metrics, dashboards, analysis and decision-support systems.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: Business/domain understanding matters alongside technical skill.
industry_changes.source: Amazon Data Engineer India 2027; Amazon Data Science

industry_changes.change: AI increases demand for usable data infrastructure
industry_changes.what_is_happening: AI systems depend on large datasets, data pipelines and reliable access to data.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: This is an infrastructure requirement, not proof that every data job is growing.

industry_changes.change: Cloud security is a major skills need
industry_changes.what_is_happening: ISC2 respondents identify cloud security among the top cybersecurity skills needs.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: Security work increasingly includes distributed cloud environments.

industry_changes.change: AI is becoming part of security operations
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Security teams are adopting AI tools for monitoring, detection and investigation, while evaluating new AI risks.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: AI changes both defensive workflows and the attack surface.

industry_changes.change: AI security creates new specialist work
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Respondents identify AI threat detection, threat modeling, model security, governance and privacy as important AI-security skills.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: This supports specialization rather than a single generic 'AI security' job.

industry_changes.change: Application security remains important
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Security engineering and application security remain prominent skills needs.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: Secure software practices therefore connect cybersecurity with software engineering.

industry_changes.change: Risk and governance remain human-heavy
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Risk assessment, GRC, policy and communication remain important alongside technical controls.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: Cybersecurity is not only tooling.

industry_changes.change: Cloud-native adoption is mature
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Cloud-native platforms and Kubernetes are established in production environments.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: Students should understand containers, orchestration and operations rather than only cloud-provider dashboards.

industry_changes.change: Kubernetes is increasingly relevant to AI infrastructure
industry_changes.what_is_happening: CNCF reports widespread Kubernetes production use and significant use for GenAI inference.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: AI infrastructure connects cloud/platform engineering with ML.

industry_changes.change: Infrastructure work includes reliability
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Cloud roles involve troubleshooting, monitoring, capacity, resilience and operational ownership.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: Operations is a core engineering capability.
industry_changes.source: Amazon Data Center Operations; Amazon SDE India

industry_changes.change: Automation and CI/CD remain core
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Modern software roles mention build, deployment, testing, CI/CD and operational responsibilities.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: Automation reduces repetitive work but increases the importance of understanding delivery systems.

industry_changes.change: Cloud roles span software and physical infrastructure
industry_changes.what_is_happening: Cloud operations can include servers, networks, hardware, power, security and scripting.
industry_changes.why_it_matters: Cloud is a broad engineering field, not just learning AWS console commands.

work_changes.human_role: Review, test and integrate output.
Check correctness and context.

work_changes.shift: Manual test creation → greater automation/AI assistance
work_changes.human_role: Design meaningful test coverage and investigate failures.
Reproduce, diagnose and verify fixes.

work_changes.shift: AI assistance remains limited for high-responsibility work
work_changes.human_role: Own reliability, monitoring and incident decisions.

work_changes.shift: More reusable tooling and foundation models
work_changes.human_role: Choose methods and evaluate results.
Validate data quality and leakage.
Design sound experiments and interpret results.

work_changes.shift: Increasing importance as systems become generative
work_changes.human_role: Define metrics, test failure modes and compare outputs.
Design reliable deployment and monitoring.

work_changes.shift: More pipeline automation and managed services
work_changes.human_role: Design robust transformations and validation.

work_changes.shift: More complex analytical and ML workloads
work_changes.human_role: Choose structures that support actual queries/use cases.
Select useful metrics and avoid misleading interpretation.
Define quality rules and investigate anomalies.
Frame questions and connect results to decisions.
Validate alerts and investigate real incidents.
Understand attack paths and false positives.
Coordinate response and make risk decisions.
Interpret findings and prioritize risk.
Make risk, policy and compliance decisions.
Understand desired state and failure recovery.
Design safe release and rollback processes.
Interpret signals and respond to incidents.

work_changes.shift: Autoscaling and managed services automate routine capacity work
work_changes.human_role: Set appropriate limits, cost and reliability controls.

work_changes.shift: New workload requirements for GPUs, inference and orchestration
work_changes.human_role: Understand workload/resource trade-offs.

human_capabilities.why_it_matters: Translate ambiguous needs into technical requirements.
human_capabilities.why_human: AI can draft; humans resolve ambiguity and priorities.

human_capabilities.why_it_matters: Choose system boundaries and trade-offs.
Judge whether generated code actually works.
human_capabilities.why_human: AI output can be almost correct; verification remains necessary.

human_capabilities.why_it_matters: Handle reliability, incidents and consequences.
Explain technical decisions to teams/stakeholders.
Turn a real problem into a measurable ML task.
human_capabilities.why_human: Model quality depends on the problem definition.

human_capabilities.why_it_matters: Design comparisons and avoid misleading conclusions.
human_capabilities.why_human: Tooling cannot replace sound experimental reasoning.

human_capabilities.why_it_matters: Define what 'good' means for an AI system.
Connect models to products and workflows.
Consider privacy, safety and failure modes.
Define the business question before querying data.
human_capabilities.why_human: Better tools do not fix a bad question.

human_capabilities.why_it_matters: Decide whether data is fit for use.
Choose metrics that represent the actual goal.
human_capabilities.why_human: Wrong metrics can produce correct but useless analysis.

human_capabilities.why_it_matters: Connect patterns to business context.
Explain uncertainty and implications.
Prioritize threats by business impact.
human_capabilities.why_human: Security is a risk decision, not only detection.

human_capabilities.why_it_matters: Reason about how systems can be attacked.
Choose containment and recovery actions.
Translate risk into controls and policies.
Explain risks to non-security teams.
human_capabilities.why_human: Security controls fail when people cannot act on them.

human_capabilities.why_it_matters: Balance reliability, cost, performance and complexity.
human_capabilities.why_human: Cloud offers options; engineers choose trade-offs.

human_capabilities.why_it_matters: Diagnose failures across distributed systems.
human_capabilities.why_human: Automation helps detect; engineers investigate and recover.

human_capabilities.why_it_matters: Balance resource usage against service requirements.
Create reusable internal infrastructure for teams.
Decide when automation is safe.
human_capabilities.why_human: Automation needs boundaries and rollback plans.

roles.what_is_changing: Coding remains central, while current internship descriptions also emphasize cloud, databases, AI tools, SDLC, deployment, monitoring and resilient systems.
Testing is increasingly automated and AI-assisted, increasing the value of test design, validation and failure analysis.
Developer workflows depend on CI/CD, cloud platforms, observability and internal tooling.
Higher-level design and trade-off decisions become more important as implementation gets faster.
Software engineers increasingly integrate AI capabilities into products and workflows.
Combines ML knowledge with production software and deployment.
Current roles combine research, experiments, large-scale data and production systems.
Operationalizes ML systems, deployment, monitoring and infrastructure.
roles.evidence: TCS AI Careers; Amazon Applied Scientist

roles.what_is_changing: Builds applications around modern AI models, agents and enterprise workflows.
Focuses on risk, governance, evaluation, policy and responsible deployment.
Current roles combine SQL, Python, pipelines, data warehouses/lakes, cloud and data quality.
Combines analysis, metrics, modeling and business/domain understanding.
Connects analytics requirements with reliable modeled data and engineering practices.
roles.evidence: Industry pattern; verify with current job sample before claiming market-wide growth

roles.what_is_changing: Dashboarding and reporting are increasingly self-service, shifting value toward metric design and interpretation.
Growing data and AI systems increase the need for quality, lineage, access and governance.
Detection and triage are increasingly tool-assisted while investigation and response remain important.
Cloud architecture and infrastructure security are major reported skill needs.
Application security remains a major skills need as software supply chains expand.
Combines engineering controls with identity, infrastructure and detection.
AI creates new security risks and specialized defensive needs.
Cloud roles increasingly require architecture, automation, networking, security and operations.
CI/CD, infrastructure automation and operational responsibility remain central.
Reliability, monitoring, troubleshooting and scalable systems remain core.
Creates internal platforms that standardize deployment and developer workflows.
AI workloads increase demand for specialized compute, orchestration and deployment infrastructure.

capabilities.meaning: Write, read and modify reliable code.
Reason about efficiency and implement core structures.
Store, query and model application data.
Connect services and expose functionality reliably.

capabilities.examples: Git, branching, pull requests, code review

capabilities.meaning: Run software outside the local machine.
Use AI while verifying and owning the result.
Build neural models for complex data.
Build useful applications around foundation models.
Understand traffic, protocols and attack surfaces.
Identify plausible attack paths and controls.
Secure cloud identities, infrastructure and data.

capabilities.examples: Prompt injection, model/data risks, AI governance

capabilities.meaning: Translate technical threats into organizational decisions.
Operate servers and understand network paths.
Understand compute, storage, networking and identity.
Keep services available and recover from failure.
Understand infrastructure needs of AI workloads.

learning_paths.exercise: Build a CLI expense tracker with input validation and file persistence.
learning_paths.next_step: Create tests for edge cases and refactor one messy function.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Shows ability to build and maintain code, not only solve syntax exercises.

learning_paths.exercise: Add SQLite/PostgreSQL to a small API and design three related tables.
learning_paths.next_step: Add indexes and explain why each query needs them.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Shows data modeling plus application integration.

learning_paths.exercise: Build a REST API for a small task system.
learning_paths.next_step: Add authentication, pagination and error handling.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Shows end-to-end backend thinking.

learning_paths.exercise: Write tests for an existing small project, then introduce and fix three bugs.
learning_paths.next_step: Add integration tests and a reproducible bug report.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Shows verification ability, important when AI-generated code can be almost right.

learning_paths.exercise: Use an AI coding assistant to implement a feature, then write tests that catch at least one generated mistake.
learning_paths.next_step: Compare AI-generated and hand-written approaches and document trade-offs.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Builds the capability to use AI without outsourcing judgment.

learning_paths.exercise: Design and build a URL shortener with API + database.
learning_paths.next_step: Add caching, rate limiting and failure scenarios.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Moves from isolated code to system-level reasoning.

learning_paths.exercise: Containerize and deploy your API.
learning_paths.next_step: Add CI/CD and rollback documentation.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Demonstrates software lifecycle ownership.

learning_paths.exercise: Build a small classification model and compare two baselines.
learning_paths.next_step: Perform error analysis and explain five wrong predictions.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Shows model evaluation rather than only training.

learning_paths.exercise: Analyze an A/B-test-like dataset and report uncertainty.
learning_paths.next_step: Simulate repeated experiments and compare conclusions.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Builds evidence-based reasoning for ML/data work.

learning_paths.exercise: Create an evaluation suite for a model with multiple failure categories.
learning_paths.next_step: Add robustness tests and document limitations.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Shows ability to judge model quality.

learning_paths.exercise: Serve a trained model through an API and containerize it.
learning_paths.next_step: Add monitoring for latency and prediction distribution.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Connects ML to production engineering.

learning_paths.exercise: Build a small RAG application over a controlled document set.
learning_paths.next_step: Create a test set and measure incorrect/unsupported answers.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Demonstrates evaluation and integration, not prompt tricks alone.

learning_paths.exercise: Analyze a realistic sales dataset using joins, CTEs and window functions.
learning_paths.next_step: Optimize two slow queries and explain the index choice.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Builds practical data manipulation ability.

learning_paths.exercise: Convert messy spreadsheet data into a normalized relational schema.
learning_paths.next_step: Create a dimensional model for analytics and compare the designs.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Shows ability to structure data for use.

learning_paths.exercise: Build a pipeline that ingests CSV/API data, validates it and stores clean tables.
learning_paths.next_step: Schedule it and add failure/retry logging.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Demonstrates production data workflow.

learning_paths.exercise: Create a small cloud-style data lake locally using object storage concepts + Spark.
learning_paths.next_step: Add partitioning and compare query performance.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Connects data engineering concepts to modern platforms.

learning_paths.exercise: Capture and explain HTTP/DNS/TCP traffic for a simple web request.
learning_paths.next_step: Identify where TLS changes what an observer can see.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Builds foundational security reasoning.

learning_paths.exercise: Threat-model a student web app and identify five attack paths.
learning_paths.next_step: Prioritize threats by likelihood and impact.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Builds risk reasoning rather than tool memorization.

learning_paths.exercise: Build a deliberately vulnerable web app and then fix its top vulnerabilities.
learning_paths.next_step: Add automated security checks to CI.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Shows ability to connect development and security.

learning_paths.exercise: Create a small log-analysis pipeline and detect suspicious patterns.
learning_paths.next_step: Write an incident timeline and response playbook.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Builds investigation and response capability.

learning_paths.exercise: Threat-model a RAG/LLM application for prompt injection, data leakage and unsafe tools.
learning_paths.next_step: Create tests for each threat and document mitigations.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Directly connects emerging AI systems to security work.

learning_paths.exercise: Deploy a small Linux service and troubleshoot a broken network configuration.
learning_paths.next_step: Write a runbook for three common failures.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Builds operational troubleshooting.

learning_paths.exercise: Containerize a backend app with a database.
learning_paths.next_step: Add health checks and resource limits.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Demonstrates repeatable application deployment.

learning_paths.exercise: Deploy a two-service application to Kubernetes.
learning_paths.next_step: Add scaling, configuration and a failure simulation.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Builds platform concepts beyond memorizing kubectl commands.

learning_paths.exercise: Create a pipeline that tests and deploys a containerized app.
learning_paths.next_step: Add a failed-test gate and rollback step.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Demonstrates automated software delivery.

learning_paths.exercise: Instrument an API with logs, metrics and traces.
learning_paths.next_step: Create an incident and use telemetry to diagnose it.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Connects monitoring to actual operational decisions.

learning_paths.exercise: Run a small local inference workload and document compute/memory trade-offs.
learning_paths.next_step: Compare batching/concurrency settings and measure latency.
learning_paths.industry_connection: Shows why AI workloads create infrastructure problems.

company_cases.what_happened: Oracle described restructuring product-development teams around smaller groups and greater AI-driven productivity; subsequent workforce reductions had multiple reported factors, so layoffs should not be attributed solely to AI.
company_cases.what_students_should_notice: Use as a case of workforce restructuring + changing software economics, not proof of universal replacement.
company_cases.evidence_strength: High for Oracle's stated direction; medium for causal interpretation of layoffs.

company_cases.what_happened: Recent Indian layoffs were reported across multiple functions; reported figures and affected groups were not fully disclosed/independently verified by Oracle.
company_cases.what_students_should_notice: Useful as a current case requiring careful sourcing and uncertainty labels.

company_cases.what_happened: Amazon announced a large corporate workforce reduction while describing organizational simplification and fewer management layers; the company continues hiring and training in technical areas.
company_cases.what_students_should_notice: Shows restructuring can coexist with continued investment in new capabilities.

company_cases.what_happened: TCS reduced workforce while management framed the change around workforce/skill alignment and restructuring rather than claiming AI alone caused the reductions.
company_cases.what_students_should_notice: Important counterexample to simplistic 'AI caused layoffs' narratives.
company_cases.evidence_strength: High for company statements; causal interpretation still limited.

company_cases.what_happened: TCS publicly emphasizes AI-led services, AI agents, MLOps, GenAI, enterprise AI, governance and modernization as opportunity areas.
company_cases.what_students_should_notice: Shows simultaneous reduction/reallocation in some workforce areas and investment in AI capabilities.

company_cases.what_happened: Current India SDE internship postings combine programming fundamentals with AI development tools, cloud, databases, version control, debugging, SDLC, CI/CD, monitoring and production ownership.
company_cases.what_students_should_notice: Strong employer evidence for the combined skill profile Beyond HYPE recommends.

company_cases.what_happened: Current India Data Engineer internship requirements include SQL, Python, RDBMS, NoSQL, ETL, warehousing, AWS data services, validation, documentation and domain knowledge.
company_cases.what_students_should_notice: Strong employer evidence for data capability categories.

company_cases.what_happened: Current India Applied Scientist internship combines Python, ML, large-scale data, end-to-end system design, experimentation and production deployment.
company_cases.what_students_should_notice: Strong evidence that AI roles combine research and engineering.

company_cases.what_happened: Current roles span cloud architecture, data-center operations, Linux, networking, hardware, scripting and reliability.
company_cases.what_students_should_notice: Shows cloud is broader than learning a cloud console.

evidence.finding: 84% of survey respondents use or plan to use AI tools in development; 51% of professional developers use AI daily.
evidence.does_not_prove: Does not prove job replacement or universal productivity gains.

evidence.finding: 46% distrust AI output accuracy versus 33% who trust it.
evidence.does_not_prove: Does not mean AI is generally unusable.

evidence.finding: 76% do not plan to use AI for deployment/monitoring; 69% do not plan to use it for project planning.
evidence.supports: Developers remain cautious about delegating high-responsibility work.
evidence.does_not_prove: Survey intent is not a forecast of actual future adoption.

evidence.finding: 66% cite almost-right AI solutions as a frustration; 45% say debugging AI-generated code can be more time-consuming.
evidence.does_not_prove: Does not quantify the economic value of AI assistance.

evidence.finding: TCS identifies modernizing technology foundations, AI-enabled operations, AI governance, sovereign AI and physical AI as opportunity areas.
evidence.supports: Shows one major IT-services employer is organizing AI work across multiple domains.
evidence.does_not_prove: Company strategy is not proof of industry-wide hiring growth.

evidence.finding: Amazon Applied Scientist India asks for ML experience, Python, large-scale datasets, end-to-end system design and production deployment.
evidence.supports: AI roles combine research, engineering and production.
evidence.does_not_prove: One employer's requirements are not universal.

evidence.finding: Amazon Data Engineer India asks for SQL, Python, RDBMS, NoSQL, ETL, warehouses, AWS data services, validation and documentation.
evidence.supports: Data engineering is a systems + data quality discipline.
evidence.does_not_prove: One employer is not the entire market.

evidence.finding: ISC2 reports AI 41%, cloud security 36%, risk assessment 29%, application security 28%, security engineering/GRC 27% as top cited needs.
evidence.supports: Supports a multi-capability cybersecurity skill map.
evidence.does_not_prove: Survey responses are perceptions of need, not vacancy counts.

evidence.finding: 28% report AI tools already integrated in security operations; 19% testing; 22% evaluating.
evidence.does_not_prove: Adoption stage varies; not proof of replacement.

evidence.finding: ISC2 respondents identify AI threat detection/response, AI threat modeling, model defense, AI governance and privacy as important skills.
evidence.does_not_prove: Does not define exact job titles or salary outcomes.

evidence.finding: CNCF research describes widespread production use of cloud-native technologies and Kubernetes.
evidence.supports: Supports containers/orchestration as practical platform skills.
evidence.does_not_prove: Does not mean every student needs Kubernetes immediately.

evidence.finding: CNCF reported Kubernetes use in GenAI inference workloads.
evidence.supports: AI infrastructure connects ML with platform engineering.
evidence.does_not_prove: Does not mean Kubernetes is required for every AI project.

evidence.finding: Amazon India SDE internship lists AI development tools, cloud, SQL/NoSQL, open source, version control, debugging, SDLC, communication and operational excellence.
evidence.supports: Supports the combined 'fundamentals + systems + AI-assisted engineering' student map.
evidence.does_not_prove: One employer's requirements are not universal.

evidence.finding: Amazon Data Engineer role includes domain knowledge, metrics, reports and decision support alongside technical data systems.
evidence.supports: Supports combining technical data skills with domain understanding.
evidence.does_not_prove: Does not imply all data roles require the same stack.

evidence.finding: Amazon India data-center roles require Linux/Unix, hardware troubleshooting, networking, AWS, scripting and operational work.
evidence.supports: Shows infrastructure includes physical and software layers.
evidence.does_not_prove: Role is specifically data-center operations, not all cloud jobs.
